summary: Discovery call focused on security posture and compliance needs for Astra Lending evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main asks: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration (Okta), RBAC and audit log retention/export, encryption and customer-managed KMS, data retention policies and ability to run on-prem. Redwood AE/SE explained Hosted protections and differences for Dedicated/Private; agreed to follow up with SOC2/ISO docs and a technical workshop to run benchmarks and discuss Dedicated architecture.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Samantha Cole (Astra CISO), Luis Herrera (Astra Head of Platform), Nia Park (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Jordan Reed (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 40 minutes scheduled. Quick intros?
[00:18] Samantha Cole (Astra CISO): Yep, Samantha here, CISO at Astra. With me are Luis and Nia. We're the security and infra stakeholders, focusing on compliance and data residency for our lending data.
[00:30] Jordan Reed: Awesome. Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll handle the deep infra and encryption bits. Priya, quick wave?
[00:36] Priya Sharma (Redwood SE): Hi all, hi.
[00:40] Luis Herrera (Astra): Hey.
[00:42] Jordan: Cool. High level: Astra is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for the Redwood inference platform, and this call is mostly security posture and compliance. Correct? Samantha: yep.

[02:15] Samantha: Correct. Our big checks are SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, SSO with Okta (SAML + SCIM), RBAC, audit logs to our SIEM, and encryption. Also data retention rules — some data must be purged after X days and some retained longer for audits. We also want to understand the risk of data being cached, like KV cache, or prefix caching.

[04:30] Priya: Great — we're comfortable to walk through those. Quick note, our Hosted API offers encryption at rest and in transit, SOC2 Type II attestation, and we provide audit logs and SSO integrations; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and optional VPC peering; Private is our customer-deployed control plane option for air-gapped or on-prem. We'll go through each requirement and where it maps.

[06:05] Nia Park (Astra): Can you clarify the difference in data isolation between Hosted and Dedicated? If we send PII through the API, is it stored, cached, or logged?

[07:00] Priya: Short answer: Hosted is a multi-tenant control plane with strong tenancy controls and data protections; request payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest. We generally persist logs and metrics for a configurable window, by default short. For inference, we have ephemeral KV/prefix caching optimizations — those are per-tenant and TTL-based, but in Hosted the cache is on Redwood-managed infra. With Dedicated you get reserved dedicated pools and stricter isolation — caches are still present but only accessible within your Dedicated pool. In Private you control the infra so you own the caching layer.

[09:24] Samantha: OK, so for Hosted, can we require no persistent storage of raw request content? Some vendors offer redact-on-ingest or never persist policy.

[10:02] Jordan: We can support 'no persistent request store' as a configuration for enterprise customers — we have modes where raw request bodies are not stored beyond ephemeral processing and KV cache TTLs. We also have redact-on-ingest options for logs. Priya, do you want to add details on retention windows?

[10:25] Priya: Yeah. There are a few buckets: service logs (errors, latencies), access logs (auth events), and request/response payloads. By default, payload traces are kept for 30 days in Hosted for debugging, but we can reduce that or disable storing request/response for Enterprise contracts. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM (S3 or syslog) and retention is handled by your SIEM if you choose export.

[12:00] Luis: For our compliance we need audit logs retained for 7 years for certain transactions. Can Redwood support exporting and long-term retention? Also need tamper evidence.

[13:10] Priya: Yes — audit logs can be streamed to your S3 bucket or pushed to a SIEM, and we support signing and append-only log mechanisms — we can supply a hash chain or manifest for tamper-evidence to satisfy auditors. For Dedicated we can set stricter controls and longer local retention before export.

[15:05] Samantha: What about encryption keys — can we use our KMS (customer-managed keys)? We have strict key custody policies.

[15:30] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private: you can provide an AWS KMS key or an external HSM. For Hosted we support a bring-your-key pattern for certain enterprise agreements — the control plane still runs on our infra but encryption at rest uses a CMK you manage; for some sensitive workloads customers prefer Dedicated or Private to keep all key management inside their VPC.

[17:05] Nia: Are logs and request payloads encrypted with the same CMK? How granular is key usage?

[17:22] Priya: You can scope keys — e.g., CMK A for model artifacts and CMK B for request payloads. We also support envelope encryption so different subsystems use different data keys but protected by your CMK. Implementation details depend on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

[19:15] Samantha: SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM. We also need role-based access control mapping to our IAM groups.

[19:40] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML SSO for the Console and SCIM provisioning for users/groups. RBAC is role-based in the Console, and for Dedicated/Private we support syncing with your directory for fine-grained roles. Priya, any specifics?

[20:05] Priya: We have built-in roles (Admin, Dev, Read-only, Billing) and you can create custom roles with granular permissions — e.g., can query models, can create endpoints, can manage keys. For SCIM we map Okta groups to Console roles, and for Dedicated you can integrate with your IdP over SAML + SCIM and enforce MFA via your IdP.

[22:10] Luis: Do you have audit trails for who invoked which model and what prompts were used? Our auditors want user-level traces tied to SAML identity.

[22:45] Priya: Yes — we log API key usage, identity mapping, and per-request metadata. If you route requests through our Console or allow user-level tokens, we can include the SAML-linked principal in logs. For payloads we recommend redact-on-export if you're exporting to a SIEM to avoid leaking PII.

[24:00] Samantha: There's often concern about model caching leaking PII across tenants. You mentioned TTL-based caches — how do you prevent cross-customer leakage?

[24:30] Priya: We partition caches by tenant and by deployment pool. In Hosted we logically partition; in Dedicated and Private it's physically isolated. We also have sanitization layers and guardrails on KV cache keys to avoid accidental key collisions. For absolute guarantees, Private is the only way to have full control over caching semantics.

[26:00] Nia: We're also evaluating inference quality vs latency tradeoffs. Not security per se, but it affects whether we choose quantized models on Dedicated which may change KV memory handling. Can Redwood provide guidance?

[26:30] Jordan: Yup — Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles and we can run your workload on a test Dedicated pool to measure. That's part of the benchmark runbook Priya will create.

[28:20] Samantha: Any SOC2 or ISO artifacts we can review? Our procurement requires Type II and ISO27001.

[28:40] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 summaries — I'll send the attestation reports and the summary of scope. Note that some details are redacted for customer security but we can provide the auditor letter and architecture diagrams.

[29:10] Luis: For Hosted, who signs the BAA or data processing addendum? We handle payment for Hosted but need a DPA.

[29:34] Jordan: We provide a DPA and BAA for customers handling regulated data; legal can sign the appropriate DPA. For Dedicated and Private we include the contractual language in the enterprise agreement.

[31:00] Samantha: Regarding network controls — can we restrict egress, require VPC peering, and control outbound access?

[31:20] Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking, you can restrict egress via firewall rules and NAT configurations. Private is fully within your network so you control all egress. Hosted supports IP allowlists for API access and private endpoints for enterprise customers in certain cloud regions.

[33:00] Nia: We have a few technical questions that might require a deeper session: 1) exact schema for audit logs and fields; 2) KMS integration steps and sample terraform; 3) benchmark for p95 latency with KV cache warm vs cold.

[33:25] Jordan: Makes sense. We'll set up a technical deep dive with our infra team — Priya will lead.

[34:10] Samantha: One more: data residency. We need EU data to stay in EU regions. Do you provide region pinning?

[34:30] Priya: Yes — we can pin hosts and storage to specific cloud regions. For Hosted we have region options; Dedicated gives you region-level isolation and Private is fully in-region by default.

[36:00] Luis: On incident response and notifications — what's your SLA for security incidents, and do you provide postmortems?

[36:25] Jordan: We have an enterprise SLA and incident response process. For Dedicated/Private customers we include faster response windows and named contacts. We can provide our IR playbook and typical timelines. Postmortems are shared with customers affected by incidents.

[38:10] Samantha: Thanks. This covers our ask. Next steps?

[38:20] Jordan: We'll send SOC2/ISO docs and the architecture diagram (Jordan). Priya will draft the benchmark runbook and availability for a 2-hour technical workshop. Samantha, if you can share your data retention requirements and which datasets are regulated, that helps. We'll also propose pricing for Dedicated and Private options after the workshop.

[39:00] Samantha: Sounds good. Nia/Luis will coordinate to schedule the deep dive next week or the week after.

[40:12] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with those artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep technical workshop.

[40:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (SAML heard as 'S-A-M-L' spelled out), KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash' in quick notes. There was minor crosstalk on the RBAC mapping section.
